articles.title: Beveridge revisited: Simon Callow film celebrates the radical co-founder of Britain’s welfare state
articles.summary: Christine Edzard’s The Man With the Plan tours the country with a timely message about tackling want, disease, squalor, idleness and ignorance. A new film that addresses issues fundamental to the new prime minister’s declared mission will star Simon Callow as a historical British political figure.
body: The hero of The Man With the Plan is William Beveridge, who helped to lay the foundations of the postwar welfare state. It shows that the Liberal peer was much more radical than is usually assumed – and certainly far more so than Churchill anticipated when he asked Beveridge to draw up a report into the future of Britain’s fragmented social insurance and national health system after the second world war.

Despite its misleadingly dull title, Social Insurance and Allied Services, Beveridge’s report caused a sensation: on the day it was published in 1942, a mile-long queue formed outside the government’s stationery office in Kingsway, central London. More than 650,000 copies were sold.
Now The Man With the Plan is about to tour the country, to be shown mainly in small venues including libraries and community centres.

articles.title: Pin de Fartie review – spoonerist remix of Samuel Beckett’s Endgame finds fresh absurdity in Argentina
articles.summary: Beckett’s masterpiece is given a postmodern cinema slant, with characters in different locations, music and humour in a free and fanciful interpretation. Remember remixes?
body: Remember remixes? Where you take a song and swap out parts of it with new or pre-existing material, changing it just enough to be still recognisable? Argentinean director Alejo Moguillansky applies this quintessentially postmodern aesthetic to film with a funky cinematic remix, or even series of remixes, of Samuel Beckett’s one-act play Fin de Partie, AKA Endgame. The result feels a little retro and possibly a bit too pleased with its own cleverness, and the spoonerist title is juvenile. But in the end this really achieves something with both the source material and the remix that’s fresh, pleasingly provocative, and at times moving.

Beckett’s 1957 absurdist masterwork has just four characters on stage throughout, two of whom do most of the talking: cantankerous blind, disabled Hamm banters with his servant/slave Clov, while Hamm’s parents, Nagg and Nell, live in dustbins upstage and talk rather less. There’s an air of apocalyptic doom, much talk of drugs, food and, above all, time running out.

articles.title: Isabelle Huppert, Maggie Gyllenhaal, Kore-Eda Hirokazu, Fan Bingbing, Michelle Yeoh on Guest List as Busan Unveils Galas, Asian Cinema Competition
articles.summary: The 31st Busan International Film Festival (BIFF) has unveiled a guest lineup headlined by Isabelle Huppert, Maggie Gyllenhaal, Kore-eda Hirokazu, Fan Bingbing and Michelle Yeoh. Huppert brings her latest film, “All About Corinne,” to Busan audiences.
body: Japan sends a large delegation of stars led by Nagasawa Masami, including Emoto Tasuku, Ishibashi Shizuka, Kuroki Haru, Yokohama Ryusei, Yamazaki Kento, Matsushita Kouhei, Sawajiri Erika, Maruyama Ryuhei and Nagayama Eita. A younger group of international names is also set to attend, among them Yeh Shuhua, Michelle Mao, Jin Ha and Thai star Davika Hoorne.

BIFF’s gala presentation section will screen five films with their directors and casts in attendance. Kore-eda’s “Look Back” adapts Fujimoto Tatsuki’s manga for the screen. “All About Corinne,” from director Marc Fitoussi, marks his fourth collaboration with Huppert. Judith Godrèche’s “A Girl’s Story” revisits Nobel laureate Annie Ernaux’s most intimate memories to follow a young woman’s coming of age. “It’s My Time,” from director Bai Xue, casts Yeoh as a 70-year-old woman taking on an unexpected challenge. July Jung’s “Dora,” which premiered at Cannes’ Directors’ Fortnight, closes out the section.

articles.title: The Extractor review – Indonesian hostage-rescue thriller has surprising thread of gentleness at its core
articles.summary: Iko Uwais directs and acts in the story of a band of elite soldiers who must rescue a group of researchers taken captive in the jungle. Can an elite team of soldiers rescue a band of innocent hostages from a bunch of mean old terrorists?
body: These gentler scenes make for a fun contrast with the rather well-staged action sequences, which are at their best during hand-to-hand combat, but also include arresting interactions between the natural world and military hardware: soldiers advancing underwater watch fish swim past gun barrels; a butterfly alights on the sights of a gun. It doesn’t hit the heights of action maestro John Woo’s use of symbolic white doves, but it’s quirkier than you might expect.

articles.summary: The Owen sisters may be back in “Practical Magic 2” 28 years after Nicole Kidman and Sandra Bullock first played the sibling witches, but that doesn’t mean the first movie’s outing doesn’t still sting a little.
body: The original “Practical Magic” was a critical and box office failure before earning cult classic status over the last almost three decades.
Bullock continued, “It’s because of him, this film exists, and he never got to smell the flowers when we made it. So tonight we’re honoring him.”

“It just happened,” Kidman said. It was more like serendipity, and it came, and we were ready, and everything fell into place. It’s like in life — you try to force things; it doesn’t work. You have to wait, be patient, and we both kind of open to it.”

articles.title: Xolo Maridueña Was Not Sure Blue Beetle Would Ever Come Back, Until James Gunn Called Him About the ‘Superman’ Sequel: ‘The Most Humbled’
articles.summary: Xolo Maridueña wasn’t sure what would become of Blue Beetle after he debuted as the DC crime fighter in a 2023 blockbuster. That was, until DC boss James Gunn called him about coming back for the “Superman” sequel, “Man of Tomorrow.” “I was in Japan with my friends; nobody knew anything,” Maridueña…
body: “There’s never a guarantee with anything, bro,” he said. “I mean, you know this, stuff flips on a dime, and I know that it’s not always like a merit-based system. So there’s so much that’s out of my control, but I am just the most humbled of James and the greater DC team for folding us in, Indiana Jones style.”

“Man of Tomorrow,” the follow-up to 2025’s “Superman,” sees the titular DC icon team up with his arch-nemesis Lex Luthor to defeat an intergalactic super genius known as Brainiac. David Corenswet and Nicholas Hoult are set to return as Superman and Lex, respectively. Other cast members include Lars Eidinger, Aaron Pierre, Nathan Fillion, Milly Alcock, Isabela Merced and Skyler Gisondo.

Earlier in the interview, Maridueña said it was “surreal” to act alongside Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman for “Practical Magic 2.” He shared that after his first day on set, he was so excited that he wrote down every detail he could remember in his journal.

articles.title: Ex-gang boss guilty of orchestrating 1996 murder of rapper Tupac Shakur
articles.summary: Duane "Keffe D" Davis was convicted over the drive-by shooting of the rap superstar 30 years ago.
body: Former gang boss Duane "Keffe D" Davis has been found guilty of orchestrating the murder of Tupac Shakur - the first conviction in a cold case that has intrigued hip-hop fans for nearly 30 years.
The jury found him guilty of one count of murder with a deadly weapon for the rap superstar's death in a drive-by shooting in Las Vegas on 7 September 1996.
Dressed in a black suit, the 63-year-old stood impassively in the Las Vegas court as the verdict was read, before saying he would appeal.
During the trial, the court heard a recording of a police interview in 2008 in which Davis said he was in the car from which shots were fired, but did not himself fire the bullets that killed Shakur.

articles.title: In ‘Until the Day Ends,’ Two Serbs on Opposite Sides of a Deeply Divided Society Fall for Each Other (Exclusive Venice Trailer)
articles.summary: Jelena Maksimović's full-length debut, set against the country's anti-government protests, becomes the first female-directed Serbian narrative feature at the Venice Film Festival in decades.
body: With her debut feature, the Serbian protest drama Until the Day Ends ( Do Kraja Dana ), Jelena Maksimović becomes the first female director from Serbia to bring a narrative feature to the official selection at the Venice Film Festival since Soja Jovanović’s Eagles Fly Early in 1966. That is likely to make for an emotional journey for the filmmaker to the festival, which just seems fitting. After all, an emotional, and intense, journey is also what the protagonists of her movie embark on.

articles.title: US singer D4vd's celebrity lawyers withdraw from murder case
articles.summary: The singer, 21, will be now represented by a public defender in the murder trial of 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez. He has pleaded not guilty.
body: The celebrity lawyers hired to represent US musician D4vd in his upcoming murder trial have withdrawn from the case.

The star, whose legal name is David Anthony Burke, has been appointed a public defender to mount his defence against the charge of murdering Celeste Rivas Hernandez, 14, whose remains were found in September 2025 in a Tesla registered to his address.
Burke, 21, pleaded not guilty to the murder charges in a Los Angeles court on Monday.
A judge determined last month that he will stand trial for murder. Prosecutors have alleged he stabbed the teen after years of sexual abuse before dismembering her body.
